title: Con la abuela
subtitle: Meeting grandma, and asking her to slow down
scene: {partner}’s grandmother arrives. Use usted, and keep your survival phrases ready.

lines.en: And who is this young man?
lines.note: Grandparents often talk about you in front of you. Smile: it’s affectionate.

lines.en: Good evening, ma’am. Nice to meet you.

culture.title: Respeto a los mayores
culture.text: Greet grandparents first and with extra respect: use usted, stand up when they arrive, and let them start eating first.

lines.en: Nice to meet you, dear. Do you speak Spanish?
lines.note: Mijo (from mi hijo) = dear. Older Mexicans say it with love, even to people who aren’t their kids.

lines.es: Mi esposo y yo vivimos aquí desde hace cuarenta años.
lines.en: My husband and I have lived here for forty years.

lines.es: Perdón, no entiendo. ¿Puede hablar más despacio, por favor?
lines.en: Sorry, I don’t understand. Can you speak more slowly, please?
lines.note: Your survival line. Puede = can you (usted). With {sibling}: ¿Puedes…?

lines.es: Claro, mijo. Vivimos. Aquí. Cuarenta. Años.
lines.en: Of course, dear. We live. Here. Forty. Years.
Ah, now I get it! Forty years. How lovely!
